## Summary

**File Modified:** `JavaSource/org/unitime/timetable/export/hql/SavedHqlExportToCSV.java`

### Modification
In the `else` branch handling single-choice parameter options (e.g., SUBJECT or DEPARTMENT), the code now wraps the entire parameter-processing logic inside a `null` check: `if (value != null) { ... }`. 

Previously, the code unconditionally retrieved the parameter value via `helper.getParameter(option.name())` and proceeded to build an `IdValue` object, attempt to look up or parse the value as a `Long` ID, and add it to the `params` list—even when `value` was `null`. This could result in a `NullPointerException` or invalid parameter being added when the HQL report parameter was not actually supplied/selected.

The fix guards against this by only constructing and adding the `IdValue` object (with its lookup/parsing logic) when `value` is non-null, skipping the parameter entirely otherwise.

### Relationship
This is a single, self-contained change within one file/method. There is no cross-file relationship—the fix simply adds a null-check guard around existing logic that constructs parameter values for CSV export of HQL reports, preventing null parameter values from causing errors or incorrect entries in the `params` list when exporting.
